transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~60m | Attendees: Jordan Miller (Redwood AE), Mark Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Gomez (CTO - OptiRetail), Ravi Singh (Lead ML Eng - OptiRetail), Marta Lopez (Infra Eng - OptiRetail)

Summary (auto): Deep technical review of Dedicated vs Hosted modes focused on runtime perf and operational constraints. Action items and next steps captured.

00:00 Jordan Miller: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we wanted to go through dedicated vs hosted specifically for the opti retail recommendation - sorry OptiRetail - and dig into runtime stuff like the KV cache, batching, quantization, and then the VPC/on-prem constraints you mentioned in your RFP.
00:12 Lena Gomez: yeah thanks Jordan, we've got Ravi and Marta on the call to speak to the ML and infra details. We're trying to decide if we should go Hosted for now and then move to Dedicated, or go Dedicated from day one because of noisy neighbor concerns and our SLA needs.
00:25 Mark Patel: quick intro, I'm Mark from the SE team, I own perf and kernel selection work, so I'll take the deep perf bits. We can show numbers that matter for your workload if you share traces.
00:35 Ravi Singh: perfect, we have some traffic patterns and seq length histograms, we'll share after. Our main constraint is p95 latency under 400ms for generation endpoints and throughput of about 200 qps during peak.
00:48 Marta Lopez: also VPC peering and bring-your-own-KMS is required for us; cannot send raw logs out of our VPC, and we have audit requirements around key access.
01:00 Jordan Miller: totally. quick outline: (1) isolation and noisy neighbor tradeoffs (2) batching and throughput, (3) KV cache behavior and hot-path latency, (4) quantization/quality tradeoffs, (5) network/KMS/VPC considerations, and then recapping next steps.

05:15 Mark Patel: ok starting with isolation — Hosted is multi-tenant, we do rate limits and scheduling to avoid noisy neighbor impact but can't offer hardware-level isolation. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and capacity slots which map to SLOs we can contractually commit to. Practically that means your peak 200 qps can be guaranteed by reserving N slots; we size those based on model, sequence, batch sizes.
05:40 Ravi Singh: if we pick Dedicated can we control batching parameters? we don't want burst latencies to spike.
05:46 Mark Patel: yes, Dedicated has per-customer batching policies and a latency-first mode. For example, you can cap batch window to 8ms and max batch size to 4 to prioritize p95. If you want throughput, you relax those to 40ms and higher max batch sizes. We also support continuous batching for small seq lengths to aggregate micro-requests.
06:12 Lena Gomez: what's the effective latency delta between Hosted and Dedicated for a 2k-token seq?
06:20 Mark Patel: since seq is long, KV caching matters mostly for incremental tokens. For cold starts on hosted you may see additional queueing under high global load; Dedicated avoids cross-customer queuing. Ballpark: Dedicated p95 could be 10-20% lower in noisy scenarios; absolute numbers depend on model and hardware.

08:00 Jordan Miller: the KV cache — can you explain expected hit rates and how prefix sharing would work in our use case?
08:10 Mark Patel: yeah so KV cache caches past key/value pairs per session. For chat-like workloads with long contexts, hit rate is high; for single-shot product descriptions maybe lower. Important detail: on Hosted, cache is partitioned but capacity limited per-tenant to be fair; on Dedicated you get larger KV memory allocations and more aggressive eviction thresholds. That directly reduces cold-kv misses and thus reduces per-token generation cost.
08:42 Ravi Singh: does Dedicated store KV in GPU memory or is it offloaded? we worry about memory availability with very long contexts.
08:50 Mark Patel: primary is GPU memory; we also have hybrid strategies that spill to host RAM with async prefetch to GPU for next tokens. For very long contexts we recommend quantized runtime with chunked KV to avoid OOM.

12:30 Marta Lopez: how deterministic are the throughput guarantees? we run large batch offline replays and need predictable throughput for SLAs.
12:38 Jordan Miller: good question — Dedicated is sold as reserved capacity slots with throughput guarantees in the SLA. The guarantee ties to an agreed model family, sequence length distribution, and batching parameters. If you change model or seq distribution significantly we'll need to re-evaluate capacity.
12:58 Mark Patel: we also offer an autoscale burst capacity option for occasional spikes — burst is best-effort but can be contracted. For strict predictability you pick Dedicated plus a cushion in committed slots.

16:05 Ravi Singh: quantization — we are worried about quality regressions. what quant levels do you support and how is quality measured?
16:12 Mark Patel: we support int8 and several FP16/FP32 paths and mixed-precision kernels. For LLMs we recommend Q8/64 for production most times; we run eval suites and prompt-based regressions to ensure quality. We can do a model-specific eval with your prompts to measure probability of regressions. Many customers get 1-2% quality delta with int8 but 2-3x throughput.
16:45 Lena Gomez: can we do canary rollouts of quantized models? we need to evaluate on a subset of real traffic.
16:52 Jordan Miller: yes — Redwood has rollout policies for canary/A-B and automatic fallback to FP32 if quality drops beyond thresholds. We'll include a rollout playbook in the docs we send.

21:10 Mark Patel: on batching tradeoffs: real-time latency constraints push you to small batch windows; however smaller windows reduce throughput efficiency. The cost per token improves with larger batches due to kernel amortization. For example, for your median seq length of ~120 tokens we might see 30% better throughput at 64-sized batches vs 8-sized batches on the same GPU. But that increases p95 by X ms depending.

24:00 Ravi Singh: what about cold start when model weights are swapped or during failover?
24:07 Mark Patel: cold start for swapping model artifacts is primarily IO bound. Dedicated customers can pin model versions to warm pools to avoid cold load. For Hosted we use local caches and pre-warm heuristics but there can be a perf hit during big rollout windows.

28:30 Marta Lopez: network and KMS — we require our KMS in our VPC and no egress of unencrypted content. How does Private/VPC help?
28:40 Jordan Miller: Private gives you a customer-managed control plane and option for on-prem. For VPC deployments we integrate with your KMS (bring-your-own-KMS/HSM) and audit logs remain in your environment. We'll share architecture diagrams; there's a small ops footprint for on-prem install.

32:15 Mark Patel: one operational note: prefix/KV caching improves latency but introduces session affinity to keep caches warm. On Dedicated with multiple GPU workers you can pick either session pinning or distributed KV with warm marshaling. If you need strict routing for compliance we can pin sessions to specific hosts in your VPC.

35:40 Lena Gomez: cost discussion is important — can you explain unit economics differences?
35:46 Jordan Miller: Hosted charges per-token and embeddings with tiered pricing. Dedicated has a fixed monthly reserved capacity cost plus lower per-token variable costs for bursts above commit. For heavy sustained throughput Dedicated usually reduces per-token cost and gives predictable spend. We'll include a worked example for your estimated traffic.

40:10 Ravi Singh: anything about model compilation and kernels — if we change models often how much tuning is needed?
40:18 Mark Patel: runtime has a compilation/pass that selects kernels and optimized paths per model arch and seq length. For new model variants we sometimes need a one-off kernel tuning pass; that can be automated but some hand-tuning speeds up production. On Dedicated we can pre-compile and ship optimized kernels to your pool.

45:00 Jordan Miller: recap quick — OptiRetail priorities: p95 < 400ms, 200 qps peak, KMS/VPC requirement, controlled rollout for quantization. Agreed actions: we will provide Dedicated pricing and SLO doc; Mark will run perf benchmarks with your traces; you will share seq histograms and sample payloads.

46:12 Lena Gomez: sounds good. one more thing — in hosted, how do you handle noisy neighbor realtime mitigations? throttles?
46:20 Mark Patel: transients are handled by per-tenant rate limits, token-based throttles, and dynamic priority scheduling; but under extreme cross-tenant spikes there is potential latency lift. That's what Dedicated avoids because your workloads don't compete with other tenants for the same GPU pool.

50:05 Marta Lopez: for pilot we prefer Dedicated in our VPC with bring-your-own-KMS — what's the typical lead time?
50:12 Jordan Miller: typically ~2-4 weeks for initial Dedicated provisioning depending on region/hardware, plus your infra team's availability for VPC peering; on-prem can be longer. We'll put estimated timelines in the follow-up.

55:00 Mark Patel: final technical note — KV hit rate is the low-hanging fruit for latency and cost. If your chat sessions have long prefixes we can save a lot by preserving KV across requests and tuning eviction. We'll show hit/miss tradeoffs in the benchmark results.
55:25 Jordan Miller: ok thanks everyone, we'll record action items in CRM and follow up. Expect the pricing + SLO doc from me, and Mark's benchmark report in the next week.
55:38 Lena Gomez: thanks team that was helpful.
55:41 Ravi Singh: appreciate it, bye.
55:43 Marta Lopez: bye
